stories.title: Ann Arbor City Council approves worship harassment ban
stories.summary: Ann Arbor City Council unanimously approved an ordinance banning disturbing the peace or interfering with access to places of religious worship. The measure aims to prevent harassment, particularly targeting protestors who have demonstrated outside Temple Beth Israel for decades, while not restricting sidewalk picketing.

photo.alt: Temple Beth Israel in Ann Arbor.

stories.title: Ann Arbor Summer Festival's Top of the Park to return to 21-day season next year
stories.summary: The Ann Arbor Summer Festival's Top of the Park plans to return to a 21-day season next year, extending from its recent 15-day format. This expansion is attributed to reduced operational costs, including equipment purchases, making longer seasons financially viable, though additional philanthropic support is needed for overall sustainability.

photo.alt: Top of the Park at the Ann Arbor Summer Festival.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor Summer Festival's Top of the Park to return to 21-day season next year
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor Summer Festival’s Top of the Park will expand back to a 21-day season next year after five years of 15-day seasons. Despite the expansion, the festival continues to face ongoing financial challenges.

stories.title: Employees of Ann Arbor restaurant file federal lawsuit claiming wage theft
stories.summary: A federal class action lawsuit has been filed against Anna's House restaurant in Ann Arbor, alleging wage theft, failure to pay minimum and overtime wages, and improper tip sharing. The lawsuit, initially filed by a former server, could expand to include up to 500 workers from 13 statewide locations.

stories.title: Families of 13 children sue hospitals, Michigan doctor over alleged misuse of pediatric medical images
stories.summary: Families of 13 children are suing a Michigan pediatric urologist and two hospitals, alleging the doctor improperly photographed and recorded children's genitals, transferring images to personal accounts. The lawsuit claims hospitals failed to protect patients, with some alleged victims being infants and toddlers. An FBI affidavit cited thousands of files, including child pornography, in the doctor's cloud account.
entities: Mercy Health – St. Vincent Medical Center

photo.alt: Families of 13 children sue hospitals, Michigan doctor over alleged misuse of pediatric medical images

The lawsuit claims the hospitals failed to implement necessary safeguards to protect young patients from exploitation during medical examinations and surgeries.

stories.title: Controversial Scarecrow Goes Missing
stories.summary: A controversial "Rocky Horror Picture Show" themed scarecrow, sponsored by LGBTQ+ advocacy group PFLAG, was stolen from Plymouth's Kellogg Park around October 16. The scarecrow, which depicted Tim Curry's Dr. Frank-N-Furter, had drawn complaints for its costume and accompanying sign, but also significant community support.

photo.alt: Sisters Patricia Macdonnell and Mary Ann Ramsey posing with the Tim Curry scarecrow in Kellogg Park.

inputFacts.title: Controversial Scarecrow Goes Missing
inputFacts.summary: A scarecrow depicting Dr. Frank-N-Furter from The Rocky Horror Picture Show, sponsored by PFLAG for Plymouth's annual Scarecrows in the Park event, was stolen from Kellogg Park on October 16. The display had previously sparked controversy and community debate regarding its appropriateness for a public park, though it also garnered significant support.

stories.title: $250,000 investment from KeyBank Foundation to expand warming center and support for homeless adults
stories.summary: KeyBank Foundation invested $250,000 to expand the Shelter Association of Washtenaw County's warming center and daytime resource hub in Ypsilanti. The funding will support operating expenses, food, and facility costs, aiming to serve 40 people daily and connect 200-250 individuals annually with case management, housing assistance, and healthcare.

photo.alt: Left to right: Dave Mannarino (KeyBank), Dave Purkiss (SAWC Board), Yvonne Harrington (KeyBank), Alondra Burne (SAWC), Nicole Adelman (SAWC), Martin Delonis (SAWC Board), and Versell Smith (SAWC).

inputFacts.title: $250,000 investment from KeyBank Foundation to expand warming center and support for homeless adults
inputFacts.summary: A $250,000 investment from the KeyBank Foundation is expanding shelter and support services for homeless adults in Ypsilanti and eastern Washtenaw County. The funding supports a daytime resource hub and warming center at St. Luke’s Episcopal Church, providing case management, housing assistance, and basic necessities.

editorial.reason: This story details a significant investment in social services for a nearby community (Washtenaw County), directly impacting vulnerable populations and public services. The expansion of a warming center and resource hub is a concrete development with practical relevance.
editorial.localConnection: Washtenaw County is a nearby community, and the expansion of services for homeless adults has a direct impact on public services in the region.

inputFacts.title: Preschool Gallery
inputFacts.summary: A new gallery designed for preschool-aged children and their caregivers opens at Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum. Features include water tables, firefighter role-play areas, and a child-sized fire engine.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor looks to ban city purchases of "sweatshop" produced goods
inputFacts.summary: The City of Ann Arbor is considering a policy to prohibit the municipal purchase of products manufactured in international sweatshops. WEMU's Kevin Meerschaert reports on the city's move toward this ethical procurement standard.

inputFacts.title: Legacy Gallery
inputFacts.summary: The Legacy Gallery at Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum features exhibits like the Ferrofluid Magnetoscope by local artist Michael Flynn. Visitors can explore simple machines, traffic light mechanics, the internet, giant soap bubbles, HAM radio, and Morse code. The post is authored by George Crane.

inputFacts.title: Narratives Beyond the Battlefield: EMU Event Explores How Stories Shape Our Understanding of War
inputFacts.summary: Eastern Michigan University is hosting a public event titled 'Narrative of War in Life, Literature, and Film' on November 19, 2026. The discussion will feature author Phil Klay and Professor Stacey Peebles exploring the role of storytelling in shaping perceptions of conflict.
